title: Subscriptions: URL list, add/edit/remove dialog, refresh service and profile merge

controls.label: Subscriptions
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows the subscription URL list. Reached from the navigation drawer item 'Subscriptions', which belongs to U01.

controls.label: Subscriptions
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Toolbar title of the screen. It has no action.

controls.label: Add a subscription
controls.visible_when: always (drawn as a toolbar action). The item never moves to the overflow.
controls.action: Opens C-U05-008 with an empty field. Hardware-keyboard shortcut is 'n'.

controls.label: Refresh servers from subscription
controls.visible_when: always (shown as an action if room, otherwise in the overflow)
controls.action: Starts SubscriptionService, which downloads every stored URL and merges the profiles. Hardware-keyboard shortcut is 'r'.

controls.label: Subscription list
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Vertical RecyclerView of stored URLs. It has no empty-state text.

controls.label: Subscription row
controls.visible_when: the stored URL list has at least one entry
controls.action: Tap opens C-U05-008 with this URL. Swipe from the start edge removes the URL through C-U05-014. The layout is android.R.layout.simple_list_item_1.

controls.label: <subscription URL>
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Shows URL.toString() for the row. Nothing else is shown per row.

controls.label: Edit subscription
controls.visible_when: opened from C-U05-003 or from C-U05-006
controls.action: Adds one URL or edits one stored URL. The title is the same for both uses.

controls.label: Subscription URL
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Multi-line text field (textNoSuggestions|textMultiLine) with no visible label. Its label is descriptive. It holds the URL and is prefilled for an edit.

controls.label: <validation message>
controls.visible_when: the field error message is not empty
controls.action: Shows either the cleartext warning or the URL parse message under C-U05-009.

controls.label: OK
controls.visible_when: always
controls.enabled_when: the text of C-U05-009 parses as a URL
controls.action: Returns the edited text. For an edit the old URL is removed and the new one added. Closes the dialog.

controls.label: Cancel
controls.visible_when: always
controls.action: Dismisses the dialog with no result. No list change and no store write.

controls.label: Remove
controls.visible_when: the dialog was opened for a stored URL (arg.item is not null or empty)
controls.action: Returns a delete result: the URL is removed from the list and C-U05-014 is shown.

controls.label: Removed / %d items removed
controls.visible_when: a URL was removed by swipe or by C-U05-013
controls.action: Reports the removal and keeps the removed URLs for undo until it is dismissed. Each removal builds a new snackbar whose count is the whole undo window, so a new removal replaces the previous snackbar.

controls.label: Undo
controls.visible_when: C-U05-014 is shown
controls.action: Re-adds every removed URL in sorted order and persists the list.

controls.label: Subscription Service
controls.visible_when: SubscriptionService is running a refresh
controls.action: Ongoing progress notification on channel service-subscription, ID 2, low importance, category progress, no timestamp. Title is 'Syncing subscriptions… (k of N)' with a determinate bar of k out of N. After every download it reads 'Finishing up…' with an indeterminate bar.

controls.label: Stop
controls.visible_when: C-U05-016 is shown
controls.action: Sends the Action.ABORT broadcast to the service package, which cancels the refresh worker. The action stays in the notification through the Finishing up phase, where the merge has no suspension point, so a tap then cannot interrupt it. It has no user interface.

controls.label: Fast scroll handle
controls.visible_when: the URL list scrolls further than the viewport. The thumb auto-hides after the scroll stops.
controls.action: Draggable scrollbar thumb. Dragging it scrolls the list. No letter popup appears, because the adapter does not implement PopupTextProvider.

controls.label: <download error message> (long toast)
controls.visible_when: a download throws an exception during a refresh
controls.action: Shows the exception's readable message as a long toast. The download yields no body and the refresh continues with the other URLs.

controls.label: <parse error message> (long toast)
controls.visible_when: a fetched body raises a JSON parse error
controls.action: Shows the exception's readable message as a long toast. That body contributes no profiles and the other bodies are still merged.

rules.statement: The OK button stays enabled only while the field text parses as a URL.

examples.given: the edit dialog is open with an empty field
examples.then: OK is disabled and the field shows a parse error

examples.given: the field holds 'https://example.com/sub'
examples.then: OK is enabled and the error is empty

rules.statement: An http URL shows the cleartext warning and still allows OK.

examples.given: the field holds 'http://example.com/sub'
examples.then: the error reads 'Cleartext HTTP traffic is insecure' and OK is enabled

examples.given: the field holds 'https://example.com/sub'
examples.then: no warning is shown

rules.statement: A text that does not parse shows the platform message as the field error and disables OK.

examples.given: the field holds 'example.com'
examples.then: the error shows the MalformedURLException message and OK is disabled

examples.given: the field holds 'https://cdn.example.org/list.json'
examples.then: OK is enabled and the field error is empty

rules.statement: The URL check accepts any scheme with a handler, such as ftp or file, not only http and https.

examples.given: the field holds 'ftp://example.com/list'
examples.then: OK is enabled and no message is shown

examples.given: the field holds 'foo://example.com'
examples.then: OK is disabled because the protocol has no handler

examples.given: the field holds 'file:///sdcard/subscription.json'
examples.then: OK is enabled and no message is shown, because the platform has a handler for the file scheme

rules.statement: The dialog title is Edit subscription when adding a URL as well as when editing one.

examples.given: the list is empty
examples.when: the actor taps Add a subscription
examples.then: the dialog is titled 'Edit subscription'

examples.given: the list holds one stored URL
examples.then: the dialog is titled 'Edit subscription' and the field holds that URL

rules.statement: The Remove button appears only when the dialog was opened for a stored URL.

examples.given: the add dialog opened from the menu
examples.then: there is no Remove button

examples.given: a stored URL was tapped
examples.then: Remove is the neutral button

rules.statement: OK on an edited URL removes the old URL and inserts the edited one in sorted order.

examples.given: the row URL is 'https://a.example/x'
examples.when: the actor edits it to 'https://b.example/y' and taps OK
examples.then: the old URL is gone, the new one is listed at its sorted position and the list scrolls to it

examples.given: the list holds 'https://a.example/x' and 'https://b.example/y'
examples.when: the actor edits 'https://b.example/y' to 'https://a.example/x' and taps OK
examples.then: the old URL is removed, the edited URL replaces the equal stored row, the list holds one row and the public store holds one line

rules.statement: Remove deletes the URL immediately and shows an undo snackbar.

examples.given: a stored URL is open in the edit dialog
examples.then: the row disappears, the store loses the URL and the snackbar offers Undo

examples.given: the list holds one stored URL
examples.when: the actor opens it in the edit dialog and taps Remove
examples.then: the list shows no rows and the snackbar still offers Undo

rules.statement: A start swipe on a row deletes the URL immediately and shows an undo snackbar.

examples.given: the list holds one URL
examples.when: the actor swipes the row from the start edge
examples.then: the row is removed and the snackbar appears

examples.given: the list holds one URL
examples.when: the actor swipes the row toward the end edge
examples.then: the row stays and no snackbar appears, because the item touch callback enables only the start direction

rules.statement: Undo re-adds all removed URLs in sorted order and persists the list.

examples.given: two URLs were removed while one snackbar was showing
examples.then: both URLs return at their sorted positions and the store holds them again

examples.given: the actor removed the only URL and the snackbar offers Undo
examples.when: the snackbar is dismissed without the Undo action
examples.then: no undo callback runs, the URL stays removed and the store still lacks it, because the dismissal clears the removed list

rules.statement: The subscription list is stored as newline-joined URL strings under the public store key subscription.

examples.given: the list holds two URLs
examples.when: the adapter persists after a change
examples.then: the public store holds the two URLs separated by one newline

examples.given: the list holds no URL
examples.when: the adapter persists the empty list
examples.then: the public store holds the empty string under subscription and a later read lists no row

rules.statement: Stored lines that do not parse as URLs are dropped when the list loads.

examples.given: the stored value holds one URL and one plain word
examples.then: only the URL is listed and the next write drops the plain word

examples.given: the stored value holds 'https://b.example/y' and 'https://a.example/x'
examples.then: both URLs are listed with 'https://a.example/x' first, and the next write stores both lines

rules.statement: Rows are sorted by host, then port, then URL.file, then protocol. URL.file is the path plus the query string, so two URLs with equal paths and different queries sort by the query.

examples.given: the list holds 'https://b.example/x' and 'https://a.example/y'
examples.then: 'https://a.example/y' is the first row

examples.given: the list holds 'https://a.example/x?c=2' and 'https://a.example/x?a=1'
examples.then: 'https://a.example/x?a=1' comes first because the queries differ

rules.statement: Adding a URL that is already listed changes nothing. The sorted list replaces the equal item in place, keeps its size, inserts no row and writes no store entry.

examples.given: the list holds 'https://a.example/x'
examples.when: the actor adds the same URL again
examples.then: the list still shows one row and the store still holds one line

examples.given: the list holds 'https://a.example/x' and 'https://b.example/y'
examples.then: the list still holds two rows and the store is not rewritten

rules.statement: Refresh servers from subscription is enabled only while SubscriptionService.idle is true.

examples.given: the screen opens and no refresh runs
examples.then: the refresh menu item is enabled

examples.given: a refresh started
examples.then: the refresh menu item is disabled

rules.statement: A start request while the worker is fetching stops the service. The destroy cancels the job, so the run ends without creating profiles.

examples.given: worker is not null and a second start intent arrives
examples.then: stopSelf(startId) runs and no second worker is started

examples.given: the second start stopped the service
examples.then: the first worker is cancelled, no profile is written and idle returns to true

examples.given: the service is idle and the actor taps Refresh servers from subscription
examples.then: idle becomes false, one worker starts, stopSelf does not run and the run proceeds to fetch and merge

rules.statement: The notification shows a determinate bar from zero to N while downloads run and an indeterminate bar after the last one. The title counts finished downloads and then reads Finishing up.

examples.given: three subscription URLs are stored
examples.when: the service starts and each fetch finishes
examples.then: the title goes from '(0 of 3)' to '(3 of 3)' and the bar fills by one third each time

examples.given: every fetch has finished
examples.then: the title reads 'Finishing up…' and the bar turns indeterminate

rules.statement: Stop broadcasts Action.ABORT, which cancels the worker. A cancellation during fetching creates no profile. During Finishing up the merge has no suspension point, so a Stop tap cannot interrupt it and the profiles are still created and written.

examples.given: a refresh is waiting on a slow download
examples.then: the worker is cancelled, no profile is created, the notification is removed and idle returns to true

examples.given: the notification reads 'Finishing up…'
examples.then: the merge runs to completion on the main thread, the profiles are written, and the finally block only cancels the notification and sets idle true

rules.statement: A failed download shows a long toast with the platform message and yields no body. The refresh continues with the other URLs, and the merge still marks every Active non-user profile Obsolete, so the profiles of that URL leave the profile list unless another body lists them.

examples.given: one of two URLs cannot be reached
examples.then: a long toast shows the error, the other URL is still processed and the profiles of the failing URL become Obsolete

examples.given: a URL that cannot be reached created three Active profiles
examples.then: the three profiles are Obsolete and absent from the profile list until a body lists them again

examples.given: two stored URLs are both reachable and each body lists the servers it created before
examples.then: no toast appears, both bodies merge and the profiles they list stay Active

rules.statement: A body that raises a JSON parse error shows a long toast and contributes no profiles. The other bodies still merge and the profiles of that URL become Obsolete unless another body lists them. A body of bare literals does not raise. The tokenizer returns strings or numbers, the parser ignores them, and no toast appears.

examples.given: a subscription body raises a JSON exception, for example a body with an unterminated string
examples.then: a long toast shows the parse message and nothing is added from that body

examples.given: a subscription URL serves the bare words 'Not Found'
examples.then: the tokenizer returns string tokens, the parser ignores them, no toast appears and no profile is added

examples.given: a subscription URL serves one JSON object with server, server_port, password and method
examples.then: the object parses, its server becomes an Active profile and no toast appears

rules.statement: Every Active non-user profile that survives the duplicate check becomes Obsolete before the fetched profiles are applied. An Active duplicate is deleted in the preprocessing phase instead, so it never becomes Obsolete.

examples.given: an Active profile is not listed by the new body
examples.when: the refresh preprocesses the stored profiles
examples.then: its status becomes Obsolete and it is queued for a write

examples.given: two Active non-user profiles share one name and one address
examples.when: the refresh preprocesses the stored profiles
examples.then: the first becomes Obsolete and the second is deleted without ever becoming Obsolete

rules.statement: A re-listed Obsolete profile keeps its id and takes the new password, method, plugin and UDP fallback.

examples.given: profile A is Obsolete and the new body lists A with a new password
examples.then: A becomes Active with the new transport fields and the same id

examples.given: profile A is Obsolete with a plugin and a UDP fallback, and the new body lists A without plugin or udp_fallback
examples.then: A becomes Active with no plugin and no UDP fallback and keeps its id

rules.statement: A new subscription profile is created Active. It starts from the current profile's route, ipv6, metered, proxy apps, bypass, individual and udpdns. A body key that is present overrides the copied value. remote_dns always comes from the body or the default 'dns.google'.

examples.given: the current profile uses route 'bypass-lan' and the body entry has no route key
examples.when: the body lists a new server
examples.then: the new Active profile also uses route 'bypass-lan'

examples.given: the current profile uses route 'bypass-lan' and the body entry sets route to 'gfwlist'
examples.when: the body lists a new server
examples.then: the new Active profile uses route 'gfwlist'

rules.statement: In the preprocessing phase a non-user profile whose name-plus-address key is already taken is deleted. Deleting the current one resets the profile id to 0. User-configured profiles are skipped before the duplicate check, so they are never deleted and never take part in it.

examples.given: two stored non-user profiles share one name and one host:port
examples.then: the later one is deleted and, if it was current, DataStore.profileId becomes 0

examples.given: two user-configured profiles share one name and one host:port
examples.then: both are skipped before the duplicate check and neither is deleted

examples.given: every stored non-user profile has a unique name-plus-address key
examples.then: no profile is deleted, the current profile id keeps its value and each Active non-user profile becomes Obsolete

rules.statement: An incoming profile that matches an Active profile is ignored and the stored profile is kept.

examples.given: the body lists the same name and address twice
examples.then: a warning is logged and the first stored profile stays

examples.given: profile A is stored Active and the body lists A with the same name and address but a different password
examples.then: the incoming profile is ignored and the profile list still holds one A with its stored password

rules.statement: Deleting a subscription URL leaves the profiles it created in the database.

examples.given: a subscription URL created three profiles
examples.then: the three profiles stay Active until a later refresh marks them Obsolete

examples.given: a stored URL created three Active profiles
examples.when: the actor opens the URL and taps Remove
examples.then: the URL row and its store line disappear while the three profiles remain in the profile list with status Active

rules.statement: Cancel dismisses the dialog without any result.

examples.given: the field text was changed
examples.then: the dialog closes and the list and store are unchanged

examples.given: a stored URL is open in the edit dialog
examples.then: the dialog closes, the URL stays in the list and the store is not rewritten

rules.statement: idle returns to true when a run finishes, including a run where every download failed, or when it is cancelled. A run with no stored URL or with every download failed still enters the merge, so it obsoletes every Active non-user profile before idle returns.

examples.given: the refresh ended with every download failed
examples.when: the merge runs with an empty sequence, then the finally block runs
examples.then: every Active non-user profile is Obsolete and the notification is cancelled with idle true

examples.given: no subscription URL is stored
examples.then: the merge runs with an empty sequence, every Active non-user profile is Obsolete and idle becomes true

rules.statement: The service reads the subscription URL list once, when it starts.

examples.given: a URL is added after the refresh started
examples.then: the new URL is not fetched in this run

examples.given: two URLs are stored when the refresh starts
examples.when: the worker reads the list once
examples.then: exactly those two URLs are fetched and the notification counts from 0 of 2 to 2 of 2

the refresh preprocesses the profile and skips it
the refresh preprocesses a kept non-user profile
an incoming profile matches an Active stored profile. The incoming copy is ignored.
an incoming profile matches the stored name and address
the new body does not list it again
the dialog opens with an empty field
the dialog opens with a stored https URL
the dialog opens with a stored http URL
the text becomes a parseable non-http URL
the text becomes an http URL
the text is cleared or becomes malformed
the text becomes an http URL
the text becomes an https or other non-http URL
the text becomes malformed
a row is swiped or Remove is tapped
another row is removed while the snackbar shows. A new snackbar replaces the old one with the accumulated count.

snackbar dismissed without the action

notes: Entry point: the 'Subscriptions' drawer item is mobile/src/main/res/menu/navigation_main.xml:8 and belongs to U01, so it is not a control here; MainActivity.kt:213 opens this screen. Android subscribes only to JSON bodies (SIP008-like, Profile.parseJson); HarmonyOS also accepts base64 and plain ss:// lists (model/Subscription.ets:114), which is why several refresh cases differ. Android's refresh is one batch run for all URLs with a service notification; HarmonyOS updates one row at a time with a spinner and no notification, no stop, and no batch. Android deletion removes only the URL and keeps its profiles; HarmonyOS removeSubscriptionProfiles deletes the profiles and clears the selection (ProfileStore.ets:182). Android has no per-row metadata; HarmonyOS adds an updated-date and profile-count line per row, and has no edit dialog. The schema has no toast type, so the two service Toasts are recorded as snackbar controls (C-U05-019, C-U05-020), as U04 records its Toast. The fast scroll handle is C-U05-018 (an image, as in U07); it has no letter popup because SubscriptionAdapter does not implement PopupTextProvider. C-U05-016 records the notification's determinate and indeterminate bars. The merge ends with ProfileManager.listener?.reloadProfiles(): the listener is set only by ProfilesFragment and is null while the Subscriptions screen is open, so the reload is a no-op until Profiles is opened again. Navigation drawer, snackbar anchor FAB and toolbar hamburger belong to U01.
